quoted_clause: The break-even against a statically provisioned 21-host fleet ($420/hr) sits at 19 hosts, i.e. sustained demand ≤ ~37.6 rps: above that, autoscaling costs more than the peak-sized fleet it replaces.
observed: The autoscaling paragraph uses 21 hosts at the 40-rps peak and compares against a 21-host static fleet, but the same chapter has already moved the governing pre-full-policy screen to 23 hosts (case (ii) with the ρ derate) and the full policy to 34 hosts. The 21-host number is only the KV/Little screen.
evidence: Ch 20 §3 states: “governing 23-host sizing … 34 at the 70% × 95% + N−1 policy” and “21 = the KV/Little screen under case (i); 22 = the ρ ≈ 0.95 derate of that screen … case (ii) … rises to 23 … the governing screen.” If 40 rps requires 23 hosts, the autoscaled cost is (23 × $20 + $40) = $500/hr, or $500 / 144,000 ≈ $3.47 per 1K requests, not $3.19. A static 23-host fleet costs $460/hr, changing the break-even arithmetic from the printed 19 hosts / 37.6 rps.
root_cause: The cost example reuses the 21-host KV screen after the chapter has identified a higher governing prefill screen, without labeling the economics as KV-screen-only.
correction: Either qualify the paragraph as a KV-screen-only cost-shape illustration, or recompute the 40-rps autoscaled cost and break-even using the governing 23-host (or full-policy 34-host) fleet. If keeping 21 hosts, add: “This paragraph uses the 21-host KV screen for cost shape only; the governing prefill screen in §3 is 23 hosts before the full policy.”
acceptance_test: A reader can tell whether the $3.19/1K and 37.6 rps break-even apply to the 21-host KV screen or to the chapter’s governing 23/34-host sizing; if the latter, the numbers are recomputed or clearly separated.

page_hint: Chapter 22, §8 End-of-Chapter Mini-Case, “The peak, not the average, sizes the fleet”
quoted_clause: Ch 17's 436 GB of KV per host (640 − 140 − 64) ÷ 24.1 GB/request ≈ 18 in-flight requests per host, and 40 rps × 8.58 s ≈ 343 in flight needs ~19 hosts.
observed: This calculation uses 24.1 GB/request, the 9.2K input-only KV footprint, to derive 18 slots and about 19 hosts. The canonical whole-slot convention used in Ch 20 and Ch 25 uses the 9.5K end-of-turn context, 24.9 GB/request, giving 17.51 slots floored to 17 and 21 hosts at 40 rps.
evidence: 436 / 24.1 = 18.09; 40 × 8.58 = 343.2; 343.2 / 18.09 ≈ 19.0. But Ch 20 says “a host holds 17 whole concurrent full-context requests (the ~17.5 KV ceiling, Chapter 17, floored to whole contexts — no fractional admission)” and computes ⌈344/17⌉ = 21. Ch 25 ADR 0017 also uses 24.9 GB/request and 17.51 slots. The difference is whether output tokens are included in the resident context.
root_cause: Inconsistent canonical KV per-request value: 9.2K input-only versus 9.5K end-of-turn maximum.
correction: Change the sentence to use the whole-slot convention: “436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB/request ≈ 17.5, floored to 17 whole slots; 40 rps × 8.58 s ≈ 343 in flight needs ⌈343/17⌉ = 21 hosts.” If the 24.1 GB figure is intentionally a sensitivity, label it as a 9.2K-input-only sensitivity and state that it is not Ch 17’s whole-slot convention.
acceptance_test: The mini-case’s KV host count matches the canonical 21-host KV screen in Ch 20/25, or the 19-host number is explicitly marked as a different 9.2K-input-only sensitivity.

page_hint: Chapter 22, §8 End-of-Chapter Mini-Case, “The decision the team must make”
quoted_clause: a homogeneous cluster sized at ~17–19 hosts clears both budgets (prefill- or KV-bound depending on the KV budget, with a 21-host build carrying the margin)
observed: The 17–19 host range mixes two non-canonical sensitivities: 17 is the 40%-MFU linear-only prefill floor, and 19 comes from the 24.1 GB/request input-only KV calculation. The canonical whole-slot KV screen is 21 hosts, and the case-(ii) prefill screen is 22 raw / 23 with the ρ derate. As written, the sentence can make a reader think 17–19 hosts may clear the canonical peak.
evidence: Ch 22 mini-case: 40 × 1.288 = 51.5 PFLOP/s; 51.5 / (7.91 × 0.40) ≈ 16.3 → 17 hosts. The same section’s KV calculation using 24.1 GB gives ~19 hosts. Ch 20 canonical screens: KV 21, case-(ii) prefill 22 raw / 23 with ρ, full policy 34.
root_cause: Local sensitivity values are presented alongside the canonical screen without enough separation.
correction: Reword to: “A 17–19 host range appears only under the 40%-MFU linear-only prefill sensitivity and the 9.2K-input-only KV sensitivity; the canonical whole-slot KV screen is 21 hosts, and the case-(ii) prefill screen is 22 raw / 23 with the ρ derate. A 21-host build is therefore the canonical KV margin, not a small add-on to a 17–19 host design.”
acceptance_test: The text no longer implies that 17–19 hosts can clear the canonical peak; it distinguishes sensitivities from the canonical 21/22/23 screens.

page_hint: Chapter 25, Architect’s Question and ADR 0016 Consequences
quoted_clause: Accepted, this record sets the canonical deployment's precision label to BF16; because FP16 and BF16 are both 2 B/parameter, every footprint, KV and cost figure in this handbook is unchanged.
observed: The chapter opening calls the canonical system “a 70B dense FP16 deployment (FP16 label; see ADR 0016),” but ADR 0016 says the accepted record sets the canonical deployment’s precision label to BF16. This leaves the reader unsure whether the canonical label is FP16, BF16, or a generic 16-bit label.
evidence: Both clauses are in Chapter 25. If ADR 0016 is accepted, the runtime precision is BF16. If the book continues to use “FP16” as a shorthand for 16-bit footprint arithmetic, that convention should be stated explicitly rather than contradicted by “sets the canonical deployment's precision label to BF16.”
root_cause: Ambiguity between “FP16 as a 16-bit footprint label” and “BF16 as the chosen runtime precision.”
correction: Align the two statements. For example: opening: “a 70B dense 16-bit deployment (BF16 per ADR 0016; FP16/BF16 footprints are identical, so the book’s 16-bit arithmetic is unchanged)”; or ADR 0016: “sets the canonical runtime precision to BF16; the book’s 16-bit footprint label remains FP16/BF16-equivalent.” Ensure all “FP16 deployment” references are either qualified or changed to “16-bit (BF16).”
acceptance_test: A reader can state unambiguously whether the canonical deployment is labeled FP16, BF16, or 16-bit, and why the arithmetic is unchanged.

page_hint: Chapter 25, §3 Worked Example: Model-Shape ADR, ADR 0016 Context
quoted_clause: each serving host is an 8×H100 node (640 GB), and the canonical fleet is 21 hosts at peak.
observed: 21 hosts is the KV-screen host count. Ch 20’s governing pre-full-policy screen is 23 hosts (case (ii) with the ρ derate), and the full policy is 34 hosts. Calling 21 “the canonical fleet” without qualification can contradict the more complete screen set in ADR 0015 R1.
evidence: Ch 20: “governing 23-host sizing … 34 at the 70% × 95% + N−1 policy.” Ch 25 ADR 0015 R1: “21 hosts (KV, case-independent); prefill screen 19 case (i) / 22 case (ii); 70% × 95% + N−1 policy: 32 (KV screen) / 34 (case (ii) prefill screen).”
root_cause: Using the KV-screen headline as if it were the full canonical fleet size.
correction: Change to: “the canonical single-region KV-screen fleet is 21 hosts at peak (23 under the case-(ii) ρ-derated prefill screen, 32/34 under the full policy; see ADR 0015 R1),” or “a 21-host KV-screen baseline.”
acceptance_test: The ADR 0016 context does not imply that 21 is the only or final canonical fleet size.

page_hint: Chapter 20, §3 Worked Example, after KV-residency bound and in Simultaneous feasibility check
quoted_clause: The binding per-host rate is the minimum of the two — here the KV/latency bound under cases (i) and (iii); a third, phase-resolved prefill-compute screen is evaluated below and binds under case (ii)
observed: The text first says the KV/latency bound is binding under cases (i) and (iii), but later shows that at the displayed 2.0 req/s stress screen, case (iii) prefill demand exceeds the ceiling by about 1%. Without qualification, this looks contradictory.
evidence: Case (iii) ceiling is ≈18,210 input tokens/s. At the displayed 2.0 req/s, demand is 2.0 × 9,200 = 18,400 tokens/s, so 18,400 / 18,210 ≈ 101%. At the unrounded KV rate 17/8.6 = 1.9767 req/s, demand is 1.9767 × 9,200 ≈ 18,186 tokens/s, which is below 18,210. Thus case (iii) is non-binding at the exact KV rate but not at the rounded 2.0 stress screen.
root_cause: Conflating the displayed ~2.0 req/s stress screen with the unrounded 1.977 req/s used for the binding-screen statement.
correction: Add: “At the unrounded 1.977 req/s, case (iii) prefill demand is ≈18,190 tokens/s, just below the ≈18,210 ceiling; the 101% figure applies only to the deliberately rounded 2.0 req/s stress screen.” Or change the earlier sentence to “under cases (i) and (iii) at the unrounded 1.977 req/s.”
acceptance_test: A careful reader can see why case (iii) is called non-binding despite the later 101% at 2.0 req/s.

quoted_clause: The **average** cost per query declines only along the canonical 10 → 40 rps ramp, where fixed overhead (model loading, infrastructure, staff) is spread across 4× the requests and across more SLO-compliant completions per observation window (Ch 14's goodput definition), cost per request may decline until additional capacity steps dominate; adding idle hosts at fixed demand increases unit cost.
observed: The sentence is syntactically broken. The clause after the comma, “cost per request may decline,” is not grammatically connected to the preceding “where” clause, and the idea is repeated awkwardly.
evidence: The main clause begins “The average cost per query declines only along …,” but the later “cost per request may decline” creates a second predicate without a clear subject or conjunction.
correction: Rewrite as: “The average cost per query may decline only along the canonical 10 → 40 rps ramp, where fixed overhead (model loading, infrastructure, staff) is spread across 4× the requests and across more SLO-compliant completions per observation window (Ch 14's goodput definition). Even then, cost per request may decline only until additional capacity steps dominate; adding idle hosts at fixed demand increases unit cost.”
acceptance_test: The sentence parses without a dangling comma and states the condition and limitation clearly.

page_hint: Chapter 23, §8 Mini-Case, “The burst buffer, spelled out”
quoted_clause: with the ~500-token prefill included the total request rate is ~71 rps at 100% MFU (~21–28 rps at 30–40% MFU), so r = 50 in the worked example below is an optimistic decode-only illustration
observed: r = 50 is a total request-rate assumption (requests per second), not a decode-only rate. It is below the 100%-MFU total ceiling of ~71 rps and above the 30–40% MFU total range, so calling it “decode-only” is misleading.
evidence: The preceding sentence defines the total request rate including prefill as ~71 rps at 100% MFU. The worked example then uses r = 50 as the service rate for total requests during the burst: 200 arrivals in 1 s, 50 served during the burst, 150 queued.
correction: Change to: “so r = 50 in the worked example below is an optimistic total-rate illustration (below the 100%-MFU total ceiling of ~71 rps but above the 30–40% MFU total range); the measured per-host total rate must replace it before the burst budget is trusted.”
acceptance_test: The text no longer implies that r = 50 is a decode-only token or request rate.

quoted_clause: At batch 1 the weight read dominates a decode step: 140 GB of weights against ~24.9 GB of KV, so the KV read is a secondary ~15% term (~15% of batch-1 decode reads; halving it cuts total read traffic ≈7.5% at batch 1) and intensity is ~1 FLOP/byte.
observed: The intensity figure’s denominator is ambiguous. If the 24.9 GB KV read is included in the byte count, batch-1 intensity is 140 GB / (140 GB + 24.9 GB) ≈ 0.85 FLOP/byte, not ~1. If the intended intensity is weight-only, that should be stated.
evidence: Decode parameter FLOPs per token are 2N = 140 GFLOP. Weight-only bytes are 140 GB, giving 1.0 FLOP/byte. Including the 24.9 GB KV read gives 140 / 164.9 ≈ 0.849 FLOP/byte.
root_cause: Mixing weight-only arithmetic intensity with a sentence that explicitly includes the KV read.
correction: Reword to: “weight-only intensity is 1.0 FLOP/byte; including the 24.9 GB KV read, total batch-1 intensity is ≈0.85 FLOP/byte.”
acceptance_test: The intensity figure’s denominator is explicit, and the reader can distinguish weight-only from total decode intensity.

quoted_clause: so the monthly denominator averages ~2.4 rps, while the 21-host capacity screen is peak-sized at 40 rps
observed: The phrase “the 21-host capacity screen” can be read as the single canonical capacity screen, but Ch 20 and ADR 0015 R1 distinguish the 21-host KV screen from the 22/23-host prefill screens and the 32/34-host full-policy screens.
evidence: ADR 0015 R1 in the same chapter says: “KV-residency screen … 21 hosts (KV, case-independent); prefill screen 19 case (i) / 22 case (ii); 70% × 95% + N−1 policy: 32 (KV screen) / 34 (case (ii) prefill screen).” Ch 20 says the governing pre-full-policy screen is 23 hosts.
root_cause: Using the KV-screen headline without the “KV” qualifier in a sentence that could be read as the full capacity screen.
correction: Change to: “while the 21-host KV capacity screen is peak-sized at 40 rps (with higher prefill/policy screens in ADR 0015 R1).”
acceptance_test: The sentence no longer implies that 21 hosts is the only or final peak capacity screen.
